title: Laravel Quick Reference
description: Look up a lesson idea, see its small example, and check a common mistake. Open the linked lesson for setup and practice steps.

entries.name: Return a greeting
entries.summary: Route::get connects a URL to a function. Open GET /.

example.code:
<?php
use Illuminate\Support\Facades\Route;
use Illuminate\Http\Request;
Route::get("/", fn () => "Hello, Asha!");

notes: Use routes/web.php for these unprefixed web routes.

entries.name: Send JSON data
entries.summary: The response helper can make JSON. Open GET /book.

example.code:
<?php
use Illuminate\Support\Facades\Route;
use Illuminate\Http\Request;
Route::get("/book", fn () => response()->json(["title" => "Moon Trip", "pages" => 24]));

notes: Use a JSON response when sending data rather than HTML.

entries.name: Read a name in the path
entries.summary: Curly braces mark a route input. Open GET /hello/Ravi.

example.code:
<?php
use Illuminate\Support\Facades\Route;
use Illuminate\Http\Request;
Route::get("/hello/{name}", fn (string $name) => response("Hi, " . $name . "!")->header("Content-Type", "text/plain"));

notes: Do not place raw user input in HTML.

entries.name: Read a query value
entries.summary: Laravel can give the route a Request object. GET /search?q=cat reads the query value.

example.code:
<?php
use Illuminate\Support\Facades\Route;
use Illuminate\Http\Request;
Route::get("/search", fn (Request $request) => response()->json(["term" => $request->query("q", "")]));

notes: Query inputs should be checked before important use.

entries.name: Limit a route input
entries.summary: whereNumber only matches numeric path text. Open GET /double/4.

example.code:
<?php
use Illuminate\Support\Facades\Route;
use Illuminate\Http\Request;
Route::get("/double/{n}", fn (string $n) => response()->json(["answer" => (int) $n * 2]))->whereNumber("n");

notes: A route rule checks matching; it does not set every business limit.

entries.name: Build a URL from a name
entries.summary: name gives a route a reusable label. GET /link builds a relative URL to that named route.

example.code:
<?php
use Illuminate\Support\Facades\Route;
use Illuminate\Http\Request;
Route::get("/hello/{name}", fn (string $name) => $name)->name("hello");
Route::get("/link", fn () => route("hello", ["name" => "Asha"], false));

notes: The route input key must match the placeholder name.

entries.name: Send a client to another page
entries.summary: redirect makes an HTTP redirect. A browser following GET /start reaches /hello.

example.code:
<?php
use Illuminate\Support\Facades\Route;
use Illuminate\Http\Request;
Route::get("/start", fn () => redirect("/hello"));
Route::get("/hello", fn () => "Welcome");

notes: A redirect tells the client to make a new request.

entries.name: Report a missing item
entries.summary: A JSON response can include an error status. Open GET /missing.

example.code:
<?php
use Illuminate\Support\Facades\Route;
use Illuminate\Http\Request;
Route::get("/missing", fn () => response()->json(["error" => "Book not found"], 404));

notes: An error message should use an appropriate error status.

entries.name: Set a cache rule
entries.summary: The header method adds response metadata. GET /note has a no-store rule.

example.code:
<?php
use Illuminate\Support\Facades\Route;
use Illuminate\Http\Request;
Route::get("/note", fn () => response("Practice note")->header("Cache-Control", "no-store"));

notes: A header is separate from the response body.

entries.name: Filter a collection
entries.summary: A collection wraps values with useful methods. GET /scores filters scores and resets their numeric keys.

example.code:
<?php
use Illuminate\Support\Facades\Route;
use Illuminate\Http\Request;
Route::get("/scores", fn () => response()->json(collect([4, 8, 9])->filter(fn ($n) => $n >= 7)->values()->all()));

notes: values resets keys so this result remains a JSON array.

entries.name: Transform a collection
entries.summary: map makes a new value for every collection item. Open GET /double.

example.code:
<?php
use Illuminate\Support\Facades\Route;
use Illuminate\Http\Request;
Route::get("/double", fn () => response()->json(collect([2, 3])->map(fn ($n) => $n * 2)->all()));

notes: map transforms values; filter chooses which values remain.

entries.name: Share a path prefix
entries.summary: A route group can share a prefix. Open GET /api/books.

example.code:
<?php
use Illuminate\Support\Facades\Route;
use Illuminate\Http\Request;
Route::prefix("api")->group(function () {
 Route::get("books", fn () => response()->json(["Moon Trip"]));
});

notes: In this web.php example the api prefix is added explicitly.
